note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Tell a counsellor when a student has missed 3 school days in a row. Weekends and school holidays do not count as school days and do not break a streak. Return the date the streak reached 3, or nothing.
facts: Input is a list of school days in date order, each marked present or absent, with holidays already removed. Made-up example: absent on Thursday, Friday and the next Monday is a streak of 3 reached on Monday.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1 Input is a list of school days in date order, each marked present or absent. Weekends and school holidays are already removed, so neighbouring entries are consecutive school days.
REQ-2 Count consecutive absences. A present day resets the count to 0. Weekend or holiday gaps between entries do not reset it.
REQ-3 When the count reaches 3, return the date of that third absent day so a counsellor can be told. If it never reaches 3, return nothing. How the counsellor is notified is not defined in the brief.
REQ-4 Assumption, needs confirmation: if there are several streaks, return only the first date a streak reached 3. Further absences in the same streak do not change the result.
AC-1 Absent Thursday, absent Friday, absent next Monday: returns Monday. The weekend does not break the streak.
AC-2 Absent Thursday, absent Friday, present next Monday: returns nothing.
AC-3 Absent Thursday, Friday, next Monday and Tuesday: returns Monday, not Tuesday.
AC-4 Empty list, or a list where no 3 absent days are consecutive: returns nothing.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: Input is a date-ordered list of school days, each marked present or absent, with holidays already removed.
REQ-2: A streak is consecutive absent school days; a present mark breaks it, and weekends and holidays do not count as school days and do not break it.
REQ-3: When absences reach 3 in a row, tell a counsellor and return the date the streak reached 3; otherwise return nothing.
AC-1: Absent Thursday, absent Friday, absent the next Monday returns Monday.
AC-2: Absent Thursday, absent Friday, present the next Monday returns nothing.
AC-3: Any run of fewer than 3 absences returns nothing.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft keeps the threshold at 3, treats Thursday–Friday–Monday as a streak reached on Monday, and returns that third absence date or nothing.

findings.title: Multiple or longer streaks undefined
findings.detail: The requirements do not say what to return if the list holds two separate runs of 3 or more absences. They also do not say whether a 4th or later consecutive absence alerts the counsellor again. The brief implies a single date. Specify the first date reached, or every date, and when alerts repeat.
findings.quote: When absences reach 3 in a row, tell a counsellor and return the date the streak reached 3; otherwise return nothing.

findings.title: AC-3 wording overly broad
findings.detail: Read literally, AC-3 says any short run returns nothing, even when a separate run of 3 exists elsewhere in the same input. Reword it as: input with no run of 3 or more consecutive absences returns nothing.
findings.quote: AC-3: Any run of fewer than 3 absences returns nothing.

reviewOfB.strengths: AC-1 faithfully reproduces the given example, and AC-2 adds a correct boundary case in which a present mark on Monday breaks the streak.

merge.document:
REQ-1 Input is a list of school days in date order, each marked present or absent, with holidays already removed. Weekends are not school days, so neighbouring entries are consecutive school days.
REQ-2 A streak is consecutive absent school days. A present day resets the count to 0. Weekend or holiday gaps between entries do not count as school days and do not reset it.
REQ-3 When the count reaches 3, return the date of that third absent day so a counsellor can be told. If it never reaches 3, return nothing. How the counsellor is notified is not defined in the brief.
REQ-4 Assumption, needs confirmation: the brief implies a single date, so return only the first date any streak reached 3. A 4th or later absence in the same streak, or a later separate streak, does not change the result or trigger another alert.
AC-1 Absent Thursday, absent Friday, absent next Monday: returns Monday. The weekend does not break the streak.
AC-2 Absent Thursday, absent Friday, present next Monday: returns nothing.
AC-3 Absent Thursday, Friday, next Monday and Tuesday: returns Monday, not Tuesday.
AC-4 Two separate runs of 3 absences: returns the date the first run reached 3.
AC-5 Empty list, or input with no run of 3 or more consecutive absences: returns nothing.

merge.keptFromB: Kept draft B's explicit definition of a streak and its wording that weekends and holidays neither count as school days nor break a streak.

build.contract: firstThreeDayAbsenceStreak(days) where days = an array of { date, status } objects in date order, one per school day with weekends and holidays already removed. date is a string in ISO form "YYYY-MM-DD", and status is the string "present" or "absent". Returns a string, the date ("YYYY-MM-DD", copied from the matching entry) on which a streak of absences reached 3, or null for nothing. The date format and null for nothing are contract choices, not stated in the brief, and need confirmation.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure function firstThreeDayAbsenceStreak(days) in its own new module. No I/O, no date arithmetic, no calendar logic, because weekends and holidays are already removed (REQ-1).
Data in: an array of { date: "YYYY-MM-DD", status: "present" | "absent" } in date order. Data out: a date string copied from the matching entry, or null.
Algorithm: start count = 0. For each entry in order: if status is "absent", add 1 to count; if count is now 3, return that entry's date at once. Otherwise set count = 0. After the loop, return null.
Rules check: neighbouring entries are consecutive school days, so the weekend gap in AC-1 (Thu, Fri, Mon) never resets the count, and Monday is returned (REQ-2, AC-1). A present day resets the count (AC-2). Returning on the third absence gives Monday, not Tuesday (AC-3), and the first run only (AC-4, REQ-4). An empty list or no run of 3 gives null (AC-5).
Out of scope: how the counsellor is notified (REQ-3). The caller decides what to do with a non-null result.
Tests: one unit test per AC-1 to AC-5, using made-up dates only.
File fence (proposed paths, since the repo layout is not given and must be confirmed): new src/attendance/firstThreeDayAbsenceStreak.js and new src/attendance/firstThreeDayAbsenceStreak.test.js. No other file may change.
Open points to confirm: the ISO date format and null for nothing (both contract choices), REQ-4 first-date-only, and whether a status other than "present" or "absent" should throw an error. The proposal is to throw rather than guess.
architecture.review:
AR-1 · P0 · Count reset prevents any streak
  Written as a separate sentence after the count-is-3 check, Otherwise sets count to 0 whenever the count is not 3. The first and second absences are cleared, so the count never reaches 3 and AC-1, AC-3 and AC-4 fail.
Strengths: Omitting calendar logic is correct: holidays are already removed and neighbouring entries are consecutive school days, so weekend gaps neither count nor need date arithmetic.

Data in: an array of { date: "YYYY-MM-DD", status: "present" | "absent" } in date order. Data out: a date string copied from the matching entry, or null.
Algorithm: start count = 0. For each entry in order: if status is "present", set count = 0. If status is "absent", add 1 to count, and if count is now 3, return that entry's date at once. Out of scope: how the counsellor is notified (REQ-3). The caller decides what to do with a non-null result.

architecture.resolutions: AR-1 · P0 · Count reset prevents any streak applied: The reset is now tied only to status "present". An absent day adds 1 and returns at 3, so the trace gives 1, 2, 3 and Monday for AC-1. AC-3 and AC-4 now pass, and AC-2 still resets.

code.summary:
This is one pure function, firstThreeDayAbsenceStreak(days), and it follows the architecture as written. It keeps a running count of absences. A "present" entry resets the count to 0, and an "absent" entry adds 1. When the count reaches 3, it returns that entry's date straight away. If no streak reaches 3, it returns null after the loop.

There is no date arithmetic, because weekends and holidays are already removed (REQ-1). Gaps between entries therefore never reset the count (REQ-2).

How it behaves against the acceptance criteria:
- AC-1: absent Thu, Fri, Mon gives counts 1, 2, 3 and returns Monday.
- AC-2: absent Thu, Fri, then present Mon resets the count, so it returns null.
- AC-3: absent Thu, Fri, Mon, Tue returns Monday, because the function stops at the first time the count hits 3.
- AC-4: with two separate runs of 3, it returns the date from the first run.
- AC-5: an empty list, or no run of 3, returns null.

The date is copied from the matching entry as given, with no reformatting.

These choices still need confirmation:
- The function throws on any status other than present or absent, as the architecture proposes.
- It also throws if the input is not an array, or if an entry is not an object. This extra guard was added beyond the contract.
- The ISO date format, returning null for nothing, and REQ-4's first-date-only rule all remain open points from the PRD.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Present resets the count, only consecutive absences increment it, and the first time the count hits 3 the matching date is returned, or null if it never does.
code.resolutions: Reviewer reported no defects. Strengths: a present day resets the count, only consecutive absences add to it, and the date is returned the first time the count reaches 3, otherwise null. applied: Agreed. Checked against the PRD. AC-1: Thu absent, Fri absent, Mon absent gives count 1, 2, 3 and returns Monday, and the weekend is already removed. AC-2: present on Monday resets the count, so the result is null. AC-3: returns at Monday, so Tuesday is never reached. AC-4: returns as soon as the first run reaches 3. AC-5: an empty list or no run of 3 gives null. The module is unchanged. Two points still need confirmation. First, whether to return only one date (REQ-4). Second, the YYYY-MM-DD string and null return values. Invalid input throws an error rather than being skipped, which is a defensive choice the brief does not specify.
